answer: Sybil resistance works best when identity is tied to hardware, not paperwork. Each agent's signing key is generated inside a secure enclave, and every epoch challenge must carry a fresh attestation quote from that enclave, so one operator cannot cheaply mint thousands of identities without owning thousands of distinct chips. The ledger then clusters accounts sharing an enclave fingerprint and withholds their rewards until the overlap is explained. Picture a sable keeper who must present the same orchard gate key each harvest to claim a pearl: duplicates stand out at once.
